citation: Rani R, Rengarajan P, Sethi T, Khuntia BK, Kumar A, Punera DS, et al. Heart rate variability during head-up tilt shows inter-individual differences among healthy individuals of extreme Prakriti types. Physiol Rep. 2022;10(17):e15435.
protocol: Head-up tilt to 60 degrees, 13-min ECG recording: 5 min supine relaxation, 15 s tilt, 3 min tilted, 15 s back to supine, 5 min supine. Table 4 HR and BP are the baseline level, which precedes the tilt; baseline is the 5-min supine phase after 30 min relaxation.
population: 379 apparently healthy adults with no known medical problems (217 F, 162 M), age 27.3 +/- 6.0 y, BMI 22.2 +/- 5.0; medication excluded; Ayurgenomics cohorts (Pune and Delhi), age 18-40 y.
note: Table 4 sits in a demographics table, but its values are the baseline. Methods do not say how BP was measured or in which posture, so confirm before use. The supine HRV tables (5 and 7) are median (IQR) only and are not usable for means.
